answer: Prism-Kernel Reputation Forking: each identity accrues a kernel of verified interaction history; the system periodically prism-forks reputation into independently audited shards, and new identities start with an onyx-tier zeroed shard. Enforcement: agents can only transact at a capacity proportional to verified shard depth, so a fresh identity is capped at near-zero throughput. An attacker must run real interactions through every shard to build depth, paying compute, latency, and audit fees per identity—sybil creation becomes costlier than honest participation at scale.
